nodes.title: Eye of Tzeentch
nodes.why: Evolve Eye into a strategic control surface for autonomous software work.
nodes.notes: Top-level project intent. Detailed behavior lives in DESIGN_AGENT_SIMULATOR.md and DESIGN_UI_VIEWS.md.

nodes.title: Build Work Graph
nodes.why: Create the planning and control surface for goals, plans, decisions, branches, and agent work.
nodes.notes: Start small; the graph should grow from high-level intent rather than require a complete task breakdown up front.

nodes.title: Hierarchical goals and plans
nodes.why: Allow a direction to grow into projects, explorations, tasks, and sub-plans.
nodes.notes: Support arbitrary depth and editable expansion.

nodes.title: Decisions and pivot branches
nodes.why: Preserve why choices were made and retain abandoned paths as historical context.
nodes.notes: Minimum decision: Decision + Why; Notes optional. Alternatives and consequences are optional enrichment.

nodes.title: Connect Work Graph to Code Analysis
nodes.why: Make planning aware of what Eye discovers about the actual codebase.
nodes.notes: Quality findings, architecture observations, source evidence, and changes should become useful context for work.

nodes.title: Quality findings → actionable work
nodes.why: Turn existing code-quality findings into possible work items rather than isolated reports.
nodes.notes: Preserve evidence and let the agent/human decide whether a finding deserves work.

nodes.title: Code changes → graph context
nodes.why: Reflect important changes and observations back into the work graph.
nodes.notes: Keep observation separate from product intent; evidence can trigger review or new work.

nodes.title: Agent Integration
nodes.why: Make a coding agent actually execute work represented in the graph.
nodes.notes: Initial experiment should use one coding agent before introducing multi-agent orchestration.

nodes.title: Give an agent a work node
nodes.why: Provide the agent with a concrete goal and context to execute.
nodes.notes: Eventually include relevant design documents, decisions, code evidence, and constraints.

nodes.title: Agent reports progress
nodes.why: Make work state visible without manually maintaining it.
nodes.notes: Progress, waiting, blocked, verification, and discovered sub-work should flow back into the graph.

nodes.title: Agent can create sub-work
nodes.why: Let the graph grow from actual investigation instead of forcing exhaustive upfront planning.
nodes.notes: Human intent remains stable while the agent plan can evolve beneath it.

nodes.title: Project Knowledge
nodes.why: Connect design documents and decision history to the work being performed.
nodes.notes: References should point to durable project knowledge rather than copy it into every task.

nodes.title: Reference design docs from work
nodes.why: Give agents the relevant existing intent and constraints when planning or executing work.

nodes.title: Preserve decision history
nodes.why: Make past reasoning discoverable when code or plans need to change.
nodes.notes: Decision records remain lightweight and can optionally be enriched by agents.
